skills.name: Rigid motions defined
skills.wrong_turn: A dilation is not a rigid motion: it keeps the shape but changes the size. Rigid means every distance stays exactly the same.
skills.rule: A rigid motion, or isometry, is a transformation that preserves distance.

skills.name: Translation vectors
skills.wrong_turn: Subtract preimage from image: A(5, 1) to A′(2, 4) is ⟨−3, 3⟩, not ⟨3, −3⟩.

skills.name: Reflections precisely
skills.wrong_turn: Over the y-axis, (x, y) goes to (−x, y), not (x, −y). The coordinate along the mirror stays the same.
skills.rule: Reflection in a line ℓ sends P to P′ so that ℓ is the perpendicular bisector of PP′.

skills.name: Rotations about any point
skills.wrong_turn: The origin rules only work about the origin. About another center, shift the center to the origin first, then shift back.

skills.name: Compositions
skills.wrong_turn: g ∘ f means do f first, then g. Reading left to right gets the order backwards.
skills.rule: Two reflections in parallel lines make a translation; in crossing lines, a rotation.

skills.name: Glide reflections
skills.wrong_turn: A glide reflection is not a rotation, even if the image looks turned. It is flipped: a left footprint becomes a right one.
skills.rule: A glide reflection is a reflection in a line followed by a translation along that line.

skills.name: Symmetry
skills.wrong_turn: A rectangle has 2 lines of symmetry, not 4. Its diagonals are not mirror lines.
skills.rule: A symmetry of a figure is a rigid motion that maps the figure onto itself.

skills.name: Dilations about any center
skills.wrong_turn: Factor 3 about (1, 2) doesn't mean multiply the coordinates by 3. Measure from the center: P′ = C + 3(P − C).
skills.rule: A dilation with center C and factor k sends P to P′=C+k(P−C).

skills.name: Congruence by rigid motions
skills.wrong_turn: Congruent shapes may be mirror images. A triangle and its reflection are congruent; a sequence may use a reflection.
skills.rule: Two figures are congruent when a sequence of rigid motions maps one onto the other.

skills.name: Similarity by transformations
skills.wrong_turn: Similar isn't congruent: angles are equal, but sides are multiplied by one scale factor, not equal.
skills.rule: Two figures are similar when a dilation followed by rigid motions maps one onto the other.

skills.name: Transformation matrices
skills.wrong_turn: Matrix products work right to left: BA means do A first. And AB usually differs from BA.
skills.rule: A 2×2 matrix M moves the point 𝐯 to M𝐯; doing A then B is BA.

skills.name: Tessellations

steps.c: angle sum test at a vertex

skills.wrong_turn: Regular pentagons don't tile: three corners make 324°, four make 432°. Not every regular polygon fits around a point.
skills.rule: Polygons fit around a vertex exactly when their angles there add to 360°.
